title: Mastra CC protocol
description: The wire contract between the daemon and its one client. Elements are named at the level of meaning: no platform or toolkit identifier appears in any field name, enum value, method name, or description. The single exemption is the diagnostic field.

semanticElement.description: One element, named for what a person means by it.

id.description: Stable identity: a kind prefix and twelve hex digits. Never reused.

role.description: The neutral role vocabulary. A native role with no neutral equivalent maps to generic and keeps its native name in the diagnostic field.

name.description: The human-facing name. Comparisons normalise to NFKC first.

states.description: The states currently true of the element.

actions.description: What a later call could be asked to do. M1 implements none of them.

diagnostic.description: Debug-only carrier and the only exemption from the neutral-vocabulary rule: native identifiers may appear here for a human reading a log, and are never load-bearing.

subscription.description: A live watch on one element and everything beneath it. Holding one means the daemon will push a change event whenever the watched subtree changes, until the subscription is ended by the client, by the element vanishing, or by the connection closing.

subscriptionId.description: Names this watch for the life of the connection. Ending a watch and matching an event to it both use this.

id.description: The watched element, echoed back so a client holding several subscriptions can bind this answer to the request that asked for it without keeping its own book.

priority.description: The urgency the subscriber declared. The daemon stores it and stamps it onto every event of this watch; it never reads it, branches on it, or reorders anything by it. What an urgency means is decided entirely by whoever is holding the other end.

changeEvent.description: One change in a watched subtree, pushed by the daemon without being asked. It is a pointer, never a payload: it names what changed and who caused it, and carries no content whatsoever - reading the element is a separate call that runs the visibility gate again.

subscriptionId.description: The watch this event belongs to.

id.description: The element that changed: the watched element itself or something beneath it.

role.description: The neutral role of the element that changed, so a subscriber can decide whether to look without looking.

attribution.description: Who caused it. Never guessed: when it cannot be decided the answer is the undecidable one, not the flattering one.

causeId.description: Names the call this change was caused by. Present if and only if the attribution is self; its absence anywhere else is the contract, not an omission.

priority.description: The urgency the subscriber declared when it asked for this watch, carried back unread.

at.description: When the daemon observed the change, in milliseconds since the epoch.

diagnostic.description: Native details preserved for a human debugging. Exempt from the neutral-vocabulary rule; never load-bearing for agent logic.

nativeRole.description: The backend's own role word, verbatim.

nativeId.description: The backend's own identifier for the element, verbatim.

queryElements.description: Find elements matching a semantic query. Observation only.

role.description: Restrict the answer to one role.

name.description: Restrict the answer to elements whose normalised name matches.

limit.description: Upper bound on the number of returned elements.

elements.description: Every element that matched, in reading order.

attestElement.description: State what a later call would act on, without acting. Returns the element as currently resolvable, or an explicit refusal naming why.

element.description: Present when the id still resolves.

refusal.description: Present when it does not; names the reason.

subscribeElement.description: Watch one element and everything beneath it, and be told when any of it changes. Observation only: a subscription reads, and cannot cause anything to happen. Scope is the point - a watch on one subtree is the difference between being told what matters and being told everything. Defined on the wire before either route can serve it; until a route can, every call is refused by name.

id.description: The element to watch, together with its descendants.

priority.description: How urgent this subscriber considers changes here. Carried on every resulting event and never interpreted by the daemon.

subscription.description: Present when the watch was established.

refusal.description: Present otherwise; names the check that ran and what would change the answer.

unsubscribeElement.description: End a watch. Observation only. Ending a watch that is already over is not an error: the answer says the watch is not running, which is the state the caller wanted either way.

subscriptionId.description: The watch to end, as named when it was established.

ended.description: Present when the watch is no longer running - true when this call ended it, false when it had already ended on its own.

refusal.description: Present otherwise; names the check that ran and what would change the answer.

openApplication.description: Open an application by name, with its readability applied at the moment it starts. The first effect-class method: visible to the person, trivially reversible. Authority is checked before anything else, and a refusal never reveals whether an application exists on this machine.

name.description: The human-facing application name. Neutral vocabulary; no platform identifiers. Comparisons normalise to NFKC first.

application.description: Present when the application was opened (or was already ours) and became readable.

refusal.description: Present otherwise; names the reason without revealing what is available to other sessions.

editElement.description: Replace a text field's content. Edit-class: changes what an element holds without committing anything beyond it. Defined on the wire before it is possible; until an edit-authority surface exists, every call is refused by name.

id.description: The element whose content would be replaced.

value.description: The content the element would hold afterwards.

element.description: Present when the edit was performed; the element as it reads afterwards.

refusal.description: Present otherwise; names the check that ran and what would change the answer.

activateElement.description: Perform one advertised action on an element. Activate-class: causes the element to do the thing it exists to do. Defined on the wire before it is possible; until an activate-authority surface exists, every call is refused by name.

id.description: The element the action would be performed on.

action.description: One of the element's advertised actions.

element.description: Present when the action was performed; the element as it reads afterwards.

refusal.description: Present otherwise; names the check that ran and what would change the answer.

submitElement.description: Commit something beyond the machine's ability to take back. Submit-class: the attestation is the machine's own restatement of what is being committed, and it is required in every call - the contract makes waiving it inexpressible. Defined on the wire before it is possible; until a submit-authority surface exists, every call is refused by name.

attestation.description: The caller's own restatement of what this commit does. Never optional: a commit the caller cannot describe is refused.

element.description: Present when the commit was performed; the element as it reads afterwards.

refusal.description: Present otherwise; names the check that ran and what would change the answer.
